00:50:25,700 --> 00:50:28,700
It wasn't me not to drink,
or dog around either.

736
00:50:31,200 --> 00:50:33,300
A lot of things weren't me.

737
00:50:37,600 --> 00:50:39,400
I want another chance.

738
00:50:44,800 --> 00:50:47,400
How about a fuck for the road instead?

739
00:51:25,100 --> 00:51:26,600
-How you doing?
-Okay.

740
00:51:26,700 --> 00:51:29,300
You unload this,
you gotta ditch trucks and trailers both.

741
00:51:29,400 --> 00:51:32,400
Make it look like it was a hijack, all right?

742
00:51:33,100 --> 00:51:34,200
Niko.

743
00:51:36,400 --> 00:51:39,600
If you want, I will pay you straight...

744
00:51:40,100 --> 00:51:43,800
or Eton can pay in heroin.

745
00:51:45,500 --> 00:51:46,800
Wholesale.

746
00:51:50,500 --> 00:51:54,300
Turn it around,
you can make $60,000 or $70,000.

747
00:51:55,500 --> 00:52:00,100
Nicky, he's offering, like,
three, four times the value.

748
00:52:02,600 --> 00:52:04,100
I'm out on this.

749
00:52:04,800 --> 00:52:08,300
Nick, even if we walk it up to White Mike...

750
00:52:08,400 --> 00:52:10,500
we can make $30,000 or $35,000.

751
00:52:12,800 --> 00:52:14,500
Nicky, come on, man.

752
00:52:22,500 --> 00:52:24,600
Half in cash, half in dope.

753
00:52:35,300 --> 00:52:38,000
Nicky, I can turn that package around,
no problem.

754
00:52:38,100 --> 00:52:40,100
-No, Zig, I got it.
-Nicky, you don't know--

755
00:52:40,200 --> 00:52:43,000
You hear me? I said I fucking got this one.

756
00:52:43,800 --> 00:52:45,100
Stay at home and watch cartoons.

757
00:52:45,200 --> 00:52:48,200
Let me handle this shit
for the both of us, all right?

758
00:52:56,300 --> 00:52:58,700
You fucking walking home or what?

759
00:53:09,900 --> 00:53:11,200
Hey, girl.

760
00:53:11,300 --> 00:53:13,600
-What do we do with the day?
-Me?

761
00:53:14,700 --> 00:53:18,400
-I gotta pick up the boys from the sitter.
-Okay, great.

762
00:53:18,700 --> 00:53:22,500
They're gonna be coming back here.
Michael has piano this afternoon.

763
00:53:22,600 --> 00:53:24,800
No problem, we'll do something after that.

764
00:53:24,900 --> 00:53:27,700
Maybe we go by my place,
pick up some things.

765
00:53:30,200 --> 00:53:33,300
I don't want the boys to know
that you were here.

766
00:53:33,400 --> 00:53:35,600
It's gonna get them hoping.

767
00:53:36,700 --> 00:53:40,300
So you need to leave.

768
00:53:56,100 --> 00:53:58,000
Look at this sorry shit.

769
00:53:58,200 --> 00:54:02,000
Motherfuckers not appreciate
nothing that comes to them free.

770
00:54:03,000 --> 00:54:07,000
I'll take it in the back.
Maybe they got some duct tape to fix it.

771
00:54:40,300 --> 00:54:41,800
-D, right?
-Yeah.

772
00:54:41,900 --> 00:54:43,200
You can't be in here now, man.

773
00:54:43,300 --> 00:54:45,800
Yo, man, y'all get any final calls
this week, yo?

774
00:54:45,900 --> 00:54:48,800
-Yeah, we got some.
-I didn't see any out there.

775
00:54:48,900 --> 00:54:50,100
All right, give me a minute.

776
00:54:50,200 --> 00:54:54,500
Let me finish up right here real quick,
and I'll go and get one for you.

777
00:56:30,000 --> 00:56:31,000
-Hey, y'all.
-What's up?

778
00:56:31,100 --> 00:56:33,900
I know you got my motherfucking cigs, yo.

779
00:56:34,400 --> 00:56:36,000
-You trying to curb me, yo?
-Come on.

780
00:56:36,100 --> 00:56:37,600
What's in there?



## S02E10

1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:04,162
WWW.MY-SUBS.CO

1
00:02:59,700 --> 00:03:01,000
Fucking-A.

2
00:04:39,300 --> 00:04:41,000
Yeah, shit is good.

3
00:04:41,100 --> 00:04:43,300
Here. Next time we re-up, though...

4
00:04:43,400 --> 00:04:46,800
tell Moe man we need about 700,
800 more of them dimes, all right?

5
00:04:46,900 --> 00:04:50,100
I ain't even seen shit like this
since I don't know when.

6
00:04:50,200 --> 00:04:53,900
-Same with the jumbos?
-Yeah, better get more of those, too.

7
00:05:02,600 --> 00:05:04,900
What the fuck is up now?
String, what's up, man?

8
00:05:05,000 --> 00:05:06,900
What up? Can't call it.

9
00:05:08,400 --> 00:05:11,500
-How's our package?
-How's it look? Shit is good.

10
00:05:13,700 --> 00:05:16,500
See these Eastside motherfuckers
over here?

11
00:05:18,600 --> 00:05:20,700
I want you to extend
to these motherfuckers...

12
00:05:20,800 --> 00:05:23,400
all the hospitality that
West Baltimore is famous for.

13
00:05:23,500 --> 00:05:26,100
-You heard?
-You want us to fuck them up?

14
00:05:26,200 --> 00:05:27,400
No, dawg.

15
00:05:27,800 --> 00:05:31,700
We're giving them 221, 734, and Saratoga.

16
00:05:32,600 --> 00:05:35,700
We keep the rest. If anybody start any shit...

17
00:05:36,400 --> 00:05:39,500
they'll have to answer to me,
all right? Directly.

18
00:05:41,200 --> 00:05:42,900
You heard me, right?

19
00:05:43,700 --> 00:05:45,000
All right.

20
00:05:48,300 --> 00:05:51,400
What are these off-brand niggers gonna do
with a project tower?

21
00:05:51,500 --> 00:05:52,800
Fall back, young 'un.

22
00:05:52,900 --> 00:05:56,700
We're gonna show y'all motherfuckers
how to grind out here, all right?

23
00:05:59,000 --> 00:06:00,400
Hey, String.

24
00:06:03,500 --> 00:06:05,500
I heard you, man, I did.

25
00:06:06,300 --> 00:06:09,400
But this shit right here,
it don't make no sense.

26
00:06:09,600 --> 00:06:12,000
You like the new product we selling?

27
00:06:13,000 --> 00:06:14,600
It make sense now?

28
00:06:22,600 --> 00:06:26,100
-Where are we at with our Boss Man?
-We should be up on his phone soon.

29
00:06:26,200 --> 00:06:30,100
-The PC is there, no question.
-We get up on his cell phone, he's done.

30
00:06:30,200 --> 00:06:31,500
We'll ID him, no problem.

31
00:06:31,600 --> 00:06:35,100
I don't know. They came down on that
warehouse phone when we spooked them.

32
00:06:35,200 --> 00:06:38,600
Sobotka's cell phone, too.
We might be going up on a dead line.

33
00:06:38,700 --> 00:06:40,800
This is the other way to go.

34
00:06:41,600 --> 00:06:44,000
Compared to the wiretap,
it's the longer way around.

35
00:06:44,200 --> 00:06:47,200
But still, if he's changing up
on his cell phone....

36
00:06:48,300 --> 00:06:49,700
Over the last week or so...

37
00:06:49,900 --> 00:06:53,400
we've not only confirmed the identities
of some of the key players...

38
00:06:53,500 --> 00:06:56,100
we've also got GPS trackers
on all their cars.

39
00:06:56,200 --> 00:06:57,800
First of all...

40
00:06:59,700 --> 00:07:03,200
Eton Ben-Eleazer.
He's the drug Lieutenant in the warehouse.

41
00:07:03,300 --> 00:07:05,300
-E-ton.
-Whatever.

42
00:07:06,000 --> 00:07:08,300
Our madam, Miss Ilona Petrovna.

43
00:07:09,300 --> 00:07:12,500
George Glekas, who runs
the appliance store over in Highlandtown...

44
00:07:12,600 --> 00:07:16,600
and the probable fence for the organization.
We followed some of them in real time.

45
00:07:16,700 --> 00:07:20,200
With this little toy here,
there's something else we can do.

46
00:07:24,100 --> 00:07:27,600
That's seven days
of where our targets have been, sped up.

47
00:07:27,700 --> 00:07:29,600
And lookit. Two locations only...

48
00:07:29,700 --> 00:07:33,300
where three or four cars stopped
at the same time for more than five minutes.

49
00:07:33,400 --> 00:07:35,800
One "X" is a dive of a diner
down on South Clinton.

50
00:07:35,900 --> 00:07:39,300
The other is on the western shore
of Fort Howard down past Edgemere.

51
00:07:39,400 --> 00:07:43,000
We get up on these locations,
maybe we get a photo of the Boss Man.

52
00:07:43,100 --> 00:07:44,900
-Or a tag number.
-It's totally cool.

53
00:07:45,000 --> 00:07:48,500
-Where did you even get this stuff?
-DEA for the trackers.

54
00:07:48,900 --> 00:07:52,400
McNulty pulled the software
from his pals at the FBI field office.

55
00:07:52,500 --> 00:07:56,100
We can pull Herc and Carver
off the warehouse and give them the diner.

56
00:07:56,200 --> 00:07:59,100
McNulty, Bunk, you guys take Fort Howard.

57
00:08:37,500 --> 00:08:39,200
What the fuck, Frank?

58
00:08:39,500 --> 00:08:42,300
You might as well
start posting them things, right?

59
00:08:42,600 --> 00:08:46,600
I mean, shit, if you're gonna run,
you might as well come out and say so.

60
00:08:53,100 --> 00:08:54,400
It ain't personal, Ott.

61
00:08:54,500 --> 00:08:57,400
I want to finish what I started
with the dredging issue.

62
00:08:57,500 --> 00:09:00,400
And you don't think I'm good enough
to handle it.

63
00:09:02,700 --> 00:09:04,700
It ain't about that, kiddo.

64
00:09:05,500 --> 00:09:07,400
Ott, listen to me!

65
00:09:13,900 --> 00:09:18,100
What the fuck do you want me to do?
Tell him where the money comes from?

66
00:09:20,200 --> 00:09:21,300
I.B.S.?

67
00:09:22,200 --> 00:09:25,900
Not to brag, but union racketeering
is one thing the Bureau does well.

68
00:09:26,000 --> 00:09:30,800
That is exactly what I wanted to hear.
This case needs closure, boys.

69
00:09:31,500 --> 00:09:33,200
And in my heart of hearts...

70
00:09:33,300 --> 00:09:38,000
I know you're the kind of bastards
to put Sobotka where he needs to be.

71
00:09:42,200 --> 00:09:45,500
One other thing
you Federals can help me with.

72
00:09:46,100 --> 00:09:50,200
And if you don't mind,
a little discretion is called for.

73
00:09:51,600 --> 00:09:55,300
That, right there,
is the district surveillance van...

74
00:09:55,400 --> 00:09:58,300
which was fully equipped
when it disappeared.

75
00:09:58,400 --> 00:09:59,500
A surveillance van?

76
00:09:59,700 --> 00:10:02,700
Sobotka stole it.
Now it's l-don't-know-where.

77
00:10:02,800 --> 00:10:05,200
The last picture was from Seattle...

78
00:10:05,300 --> 00:10:07,800
but I got prints...

79
00:10:08,100 --> 00:10:10,200
from two other places, see?

80
00:10:10,700 --> 00:10:13,100
You reported the van stolen, right?

81
00:10:14,200 --> 00:10:18,800
It was my feeling that the theft
of a vehicle from a departmental lot...

82
00:10:18,900 --> 00:10:21,500
would reflect poorly on the department.

83
00:10:22,100 --> 00:10:25,500
The thing is, I know you boys
have got enough reach...

84
00:10:25,600 --> 00:10:29,300
to maybe get the van back
without no big dustup.

85
00:10:31,700 --> 00:10:35,000
As a favor for me
having brought you the whole case.

86
00:10:36,500 --> 00:10:38,800
Motherfucking Eastside
need to get their asses...

87
00:10:38,900 --> 00:10:41,000
back across town where they belong.

88
00:10:41,400 --> 00:10:44,800
Yo, man, we run them off,
we run off the good dope so....

89
00:10:44,900 --> 00:10:47,900
I'm just saying
they all the time hustling around...

90
00:10:48,000 --> 00:10:50,800
cutting prices and doing shit. It ain't right.

91
00:10:54,400 --> 00:10:55,800
Walk, nigger.

92
00:10:59,400 --> 00:11:01,300
Yo, what's up, soldier?

93
00:11:02,700 --> 00:11:04,300
-Looking maybe to do something here.
-With him? This motherfucker?

94
00:11:04,300 --> 00:11:06,200
-Looking maybe to do something here.
-With him? This motherfucker?

95
00:11:06,300 --> 00:11:09,000
I saw him over on Ashland last week
selling burns.

96
00:11:09,100 --> 00:11:11,300
-Fuck y'all, nigger.
-Look, what did he say?

97
00:11:11,400 --> 00:11:13,600
$25, two dimes and a coke kicker.

98
00:11:13,700 --> 00:11:17,100
I'll give you two dimes for $15,
plus the ice on top for free. What?

99
00:11:17,200 --> 00:11:18,600
That'll work.

100
00:11:19,500 --> 00:11:22,500
Take it in the lobby. I'll be right behind you.

101
00:11:22,600 --> 00:11:24,100
That's what's up, see?

102
00:11:24,200 --> 00:11:27,800
The game now is that we gotta sell
more of this good shit than they do.

103
00:11:27,900 --> 00:11:29,200
What? Get the fuck out of here!

104
00:11:29,300 --> 00:11:31,400
You mean to tell me
there's a Westside nigger...

105
00:11:31,500 --> 00:11:34,900
who knows how to sell shit
without sticking a pistol in a fiend's face?

106
00:11:35,000 --> 00:11:37,000
Yeah, dawg. And you better get used to it...

107
00:11:37,100 --> 00:11:40,300
'cause y'all ain't selling shit
until we bone-ass dry.

108
00:11:40,500 --> 00:11:43,500
-Believe that.
-All right, nigger. Whatever, man.

109
00:11:43,700 --> 00:11:46,800
All right, cottage-cheese,
chest-ass motherfucker.

110
00:11:54,000 --> 00:11:56,800
-Where do you want it?
-There's good.

111
00:12:00,000 --> 00:12:01,300
Easy.

112
00:12:04,300 --> 00:12:08,300
-We could help you set it up.
-You have a surveillance to cover?

113
00:12:16,000 --> 00:12:19,800
-I got that feeling again.
-Like they don't think we're potty trained.

114
00:12:21,100 --> 00:12:24,800
-Can I help you?
-FBI. Lt. Daniels?

115
00:12:26,100 --> 00:12:27,800
He's in his office.

116
00:12:30,700 --> 00:12:33,300
Without that billboard in my face,
I wouldn't have known.

117
00:12:33,400 --> 00:12:35,100
How could you have known?

118
00:12:35,900 --> 00:12:39,500
-There was the wingtips.
-And the beady eyes. Definite giveaway.

119
00:12:39,600 --> 00:12:41,500
-Tight asses.
-Definitely.

120
00:12:46,900 --> 00:12:50,300
Lt. Daniels? Agents Settles and Mason.

121
00:12:51,300 --> 00:12:53,900
Maj. Valchek said you'd be expecting us.

122
00:12:56,600 --> 00:12:58,700
You listening to this fool?

123
00:12:58,800 --> 00:13:02,000
Saying that the Eastside
is wilder than Westside...

124
00:13:02,100 --> 00:13:05,300
'cause of some shit
about Eastside folks drinking port wine...

125
00:13:05,400 --> 00:13:07,500
while the Westside do sherry?

126
00:13:07,600 --> 00:13:11,600
Port make a man do crazy shit,
I'm telling you.

127
00:13:11,700 --> 00:13:15,900
-Butchie, talk to this fool.
-For me, leastways...

128
00:13:16,000 --> 00:13:19,400
the difference between East and West
goes back to one man:

129
00:13:19,500 --> 00:13:21,700
-Frank Matthews.
-Pee Wee Matthews?

130
00:13:21,900 --> 00:13:25,800
Yeah, the brother went up New York
and got in bed with them Italians.

131
00:13:26,000 --> 00:13:29,200
The only one from this town
got a piece of that French Connection.

132
00:13:29,300 --> 00:13:31,300
What the hell Pee Wee
got to do with anything?

133
00:13:31,400 --> 00:13:35,600
'Cause Frank was Westside. How do you
like that? The dope flowed West.

134
00:13:35,700 --> 00:13:39,800
When you got a steady supply,
you run shit like a business.

135
00:13:39,900 --> 00:13:44,500
Somebody gets hurt, there's a reason.
Not like this foolishness we got today.

136
00:13:46,500 --> 00:13:47,900
Excuse me.

137
00:13:50,600 --> 00:13:52,300
What say, Omar?

138
00:13:53,100 --> 00:13:54,700
Ain't no thing.

139
00:13:55,300 --> 00:14:00,000
You know I got something for you, right?
Wouldn't come around unless I did.

140
00:14:03,400 --> 00:14:05,500
What up, Butch?
How you holding up, baby?

141
00:14:05,600 --> 00:14:08,200
Except for fretting on you, I'm good.

142
00:14:12,000 --> 00:14:13,900
It's for my people.

143
00:14:23,200 --> 00:14:25,700
A little something for a rainy day.

144
00:14:29,400 --> 00:14:32,800
You built up a right nice-size nest
these past couple of years.

145
00:14:32,900 --> 00:14:35,800
Might be time you maybe think
about backing off some?

146
00:14:36,700 --> 00:14:38,400
Back off to what?

147
00:14:40,500 --> 00:14:42,000
Later, Butch.

148
00:14:43,300 --> 00:14:44,600
Stay, boy.

149
00:15:21,800 --> 00:15:24,200
Damn, Zig, I ain't got it cut yet.

150
00:15:25,900 --> 00:15:28,700
And turn that shit down, for Christ's sake.

151
00:15:54,000 --> 00:15:55,900
Nicely done.

152
00:15:56,000 --> 00:15:59,100
Like I always say,
it pays to go with a union card every time.

153
00:15:59,200 --> 00:16:03,000
-Turn the fucking radio down, Zig.
-Will you get in the goddamn car already?

154
00:16:03,100 --> 00:16:06,200
For Christ's sake,
we ain't got all night. Jesus!

155
00:16:10,200 --> 00:16:13,900
You could drive a tank through there,
it wouldn't take a scratch.

156
00:16:20,100 --> 00:16:22,400
Where the fuck you going with this?

157
00:16:22,500 --> 00:16:24,900
Greece. Athens, Greece.

158
00:16:26,500 --> 00:16:29,400
The hole is so they don't think
it's an inside job.

159
00:16:29,900 --> 00:16:32,000
So they don't look at the union.

160
00:16:32,100 --> 00:16:33,900
Welcome aboard, chief.

161
00:17:33,400 --> 00:17:35,000
Is that you?

162
00:17:38,600 --> 00:17:40,800
I thought you were gonna go shopping.

163
00:17:42,000 --> 00:17:44,600
-Me?
-Yeah.

164
00:17:45,100 --> 00:17:47,400
We round-the-clock with surveillance.

165
00:17:49,400 --> 00:17:52,700
When do we get to the part
where you do all kind of shit for me?

166
00:17:52,800 --> 00:17:55,000
When do we get to that part?

167
00:17:55,400 --> 00:17:59,000
So you past the point
of lifting a grocery bag or two?

168
00:18:00,500 --> 00:18:02,900
You try being me like this.

169
00:18:20,800 --> 00:18:22,300
Something wrong?

170
00:18:32,300 --> 00:18:35,100
The baby's kicking. Wanna feel?

171
00:18:56,400 --> 00:18:59,600
-Almost $4,000.
-I know it is.

172
00:19:00,300 --> 00:19:03,700
The Greek guy, the one with the warehouse,
pays me in cash.

173
00:19:04,300 --> 00:19:07,400
Keeps it off the books,
so he don't have to pay taxes and benefits.

174
00:19:07,500 --> 00:19:11,300
-And you saved all that?
-He gave me a bump, too.

175
00:19:11,700 --> 00:19:13,800
I'm pulling down $700 a week.

176
00:19:15,500 --> 00:19:17,200
You don't believe me?

177
00:19:20,500 --> 00:19:21,700
Christ.

178
00:19:23,300 --> 00:19:26,800
I was saving that up to give to you
for the new apartment.

179
00:20:00,600 --> 00:20:02,600
You know what I'm saying, dawg?

180
00:20:02,700 --> 00:20:06,100
But I don't understand how these hoes
be acting sometimes and shit.

181
00:20:06,200 --> 00:20:10,000
If I tell a bitch, I'm like,
"Bitch, either you suck dick or you don't."

182
00:20:10,100 --> 00:20:13,500
-Gentlemen.
-What's up, my brother?

183
00:20:14,500 --> 00:20:18,000
Are you slinging bean pies up in here?
You know what I mean?

184
00:20:18,700 --> 00:20:21,700
You with the nation, homey?
'Cause either you're a Muslim...

185
00:20:21,800 --> 00:20:25,600
or your momma need to stop
laying your clothes out in the morning.

186
00:20:26,700 --> 00:20:29,800
I'm here to represent the interests
of a Mr. Barksdale.

187
00:20:29,900 --> 00:20:34,400
-Are you familiar with Mr. Barksdale?
-That name ring out, but so do mine.

188
00:20:34,600 --> 00:20:36,100
And you are?

189
00:20:37,700 --> 00:20:39,200
Cheese, man.

190
00:20:39,300 --> 00:20:41,200
Mr. Cheese. I see.

191
00:20:42,000 --> 00:20:45,700
-And who do you work for, Mr. Cheese?
-Who do I work for?

192
00:20:45,800 --> 00:20:49,200
Am I correct in assuming that
you are not employed by Mr. Barksdale?

193
00:20:49,300 --> 00:20:50,400
Hell, yeah.

194
00:20:50,500 --> 00:20:54,100
If that is the case,
then I have to insist that you leave.

195
00:20:54,900 --> 00:20:57,600
-This nigger serious?
-Let me be emphatic.

196
00:20:57,700 --> 00:21:01,100
You need to take your black ass
across Charles Street to where it belong.

197
00:21:01,200 --> 00:21:03,000
-What?
-Hold on now.

198
00:21:04,300 --> 00:21:08,100
He don't know what this is. It ain't
what he think, you know what I'm saying?

199
00:21:08,200 --> 00:21:12,500
First of all, we got permission
to grind in these here towers.

200
00:21:12,900 --> 00:21:15,200
Second of all, I don't give a fuck....

201
00:21:20,500 --> 00:21:22,100
Get off me, get off!

202
00:21:23,600 --> 00:21:26,500
Pellets in plastic. Rat shot.

203
00:21:27,400 --> 00:21:31,800
What you need to be concerned about
is what's seated in the chamber now:

204
00:21:31,900 --> 00:21:33,500
a copper-jacketed, hollow point...

205
00:21:33,600 --> 00:21:36,900
120-grain hot street load
of my own creation.

206
00:21:37,000 --> 00:21:41,100
So you need to think for just a moment
and ask yourself:

207
00:21:42,200 --> 00:21:46,400
What do I have to do
before this man raise up his gun again?

208
00:21:48,800 --> 00:21:50,100
Let's go.

209
00:21:52,500 --> 00:21:54,500
Good day to you, sir.

210
00:22:03,500 --> 00:22:06,000
I'm in agreement
with the agents' assessment.

211
00:22:06,100 --> 00:22:07,400
As far as I can see...

212
00:22:07,500 --> 00:22:10,200
this case is an ideal candidate
for RICO prosecution.

213
00:22:10,300 --> 00:22:14,700
My agency agrees RICO is the way to go,
so we'll be in your courthouse, not mine.

214
00:22:14,800 --> 00:22:16,500
But I want one thing on record.

215
00:22:16,600 --> 00:22:20,200
As of 9/11,
the Bureau has one priority in this case:

216
00:22:20,400 --> 00:22:22,100
it's waterfront corruption.

217
00:22:22,200 --> 00:22:24,800
It's a new world
and the ports are vulnerable.

218
00:22:24,900 --> 00:22:26,400
This case is bigger than the union.

219
00:22:26,500 --> 00:22:29,000
We're agreeing to take on
the whole case, Lieutenant.

220
00:22:29,100 --> 00:22:32,100
But the union is why
we're in the room with you.

221
00:22:32,200 --> 00:22:35,700
If you're okay with that,
we can work the case together.

222
00:22:42,000 --> 00:22:45,600
We'll copy all the Bureau's 302s
to the Lieutenant and Miss Pearlman.

223
00:22:45,700 --> 00:22:48,700
Your paperwork should cc Squad 6
and my office, as well.

224
00:22:49,600 --> 00:22:52,300
I'll start pumping your casework
into our system.

225
00:22:52,400 --> 00:22:54,900
See what leads that might generate.

226
00:23:00,900 --> 00:23:03,200
Oughtn't you be laid up resting?

227
00:23:03,600 --> 00:23:06,100
A gunshot ain't nothing to trifle with.

228
00:23:06,700 --> 00:23:08,200
Shoulder do hurt.

229
00:23:12,100 --> 00:23:14,300
But this here work just fine.

230
00:23:15,500 --> 00:23:19,200
Tell Stack to polish it up good
and put $7.50 on it.

231
00:23:19,600 --> 00:23:23,200
Shame to let a good toaster get away
over a frayed cord.

232
00:23:27,000 --> 00:23:30,000
First off, ain't nobody running
up in them projects.

233
00:23:30,100 --> 00:23:33,500
Them Westside boys are hurting over this
more than even you.

234
00:23:33,600 --> 00:23:37,200
Trust me,
soon as our good shit run out, they fucked.

235
00:23:37,500 --> 00:23:41,300
Second, a whole passel of hard-ass hitters...

236
00:23:41,400 --> 00:23:45,100
took a go at Brother Mouzone,
and ain't lived to say shit about it.

237
00:23:45,200 --> 00:23:48,100
We go at the boy,
no telling what might get stirred up.

238
00:23:48,200 --> 00:23:51,900
If Stringer takes a shot,
he crosses Avon on it.

239
00:23:52,000 --> 00:23:53,400
Put a bounty on him.

240
00:23:53,600 --> 00:23:56,100
Let some bushwacking fiend
back-shoot his ass.

241
00:23:56,200 --> 00:23:59,100
I pin money on him,
and first thing he come at me?

242
00:23:59,300 --> 00:24:03,300
Shit. Might as well just shoot myself now
and get it over.

243
00:24:08,000 --> 00:24:11,500
There is one boy
who might could just pull this off.

244
00:24:11,700 --> 00:24:14,100
Only, he won't take contract money.

245
00:24:44,500 --> 00:24:47,600
Aim for center mass.
Make sure the man goes down.

246
00:24:48,700 --> 00:24:50,100
No problem.

247
00:24:50,800 --> 00:24:52,900
I got the three on the left.

248
00:24:56,200 --> 00:24:57,900
Fuck you, assholes.

249
00:25:02,000 --> 00:25:03,800
-How you doing?
-How you doing, buddy?

250
00:25:04,000 --> 00:25:06,100
The Samsung S221 . You got that?

251
00:25:07,100 --> 00:25:08,600
I don't see it.

252
00:25:14,500 --> 00:25:16,700
Doing the old inventory, are we?

253
00:25:16,800 --> 00:25:19,800
I hope there ain't been no thieving going on.

254
00:25:20,100 --> 00:25:22,700
Not like the problem we got
down at the docks.

255
00:25:22,800 --> 00:25:26,700
-You get the cars off?
-Sailed two hours ago on the Caspia.

256
00:25:26,800 --> 00:25:29,700
Listed as scrap aluminum.
I got the bill of lading right here.

257
00:25:29,800 --> 00:25:31,200
Not here.

258
00:25:32,600 --> 00:25:34,000
In my office.

259
00:25:38,900 --> 00:25:41,800
Forgive me, but how am I to know...

260
00:25:42,000 --> 00:25:44,500
you did not ship them empty?

261
00:25:44,600 --> 00:25:46,700
I just don't know. Let me see.

262
00:25:46,800 --> 00:25:51,800
Maybe if I had a 4.0 Megapix,
three time optical, fully digitalized camera...

263
00:25:52,200 --> 00:25:55,900
I could've taken some quality photos
of them Benzes in those cans.

264
00:25:56,300 --> 00:25:59,600
But oops. I forgot my camera got busted.

265
00:25:59,700 --> 00:26:01,600
Or you know what I could do?

266
00:26:01,700 --> 00:26:04,500
I could get old Boris
to skulk around them docks...

267
00:26:04,600 --> 00:26:06,900
keep the old commie red eye
on them containers.

268
00:26:07,000 --> 00:26:09,200
Make sure the dock boys
are playing me straight.

269
00:26:09,300 --> 00:26:10,900
-They are what I order?
-Yes.

270
00:26:11,000 --> 00:26:13,900
I got you the S series
in the colors that you wanted.

271
00:26:14,000 --> 00:26:16,100
I even got one parked outside.
You wanna see?

272
00:26:16,200 --> 00:26:18,200
Outside? Now?

273
00:26:18,300 --> 00:26:22,600
I'm just taking her out for a spin, chief.
I'll put her back tonight.

274
00:26:40,700 --> 00:26:41,900
Wait one.

275
00:26:43,500 --> 00:26:46,400
Them cars list out
at better than $60,000 each.

276
00:26:46,500 --> 00:26:50,100
20% was last week. Today, the quote is 10%.

277
00:26:51,100 --> 00:26:54,700
Still, it's good money for a few hours' work.

278
00:26:54,800 --> 00:26:56,500
No!

279
00:26:56,600 --> 00:27:01,400
No fucking way!
We had a deal, motherfucker. A deal.

280
00:27:02,400 --> 00:27:03,800
You listen to me.

281
00:27:03,900 --> 00:27:06,600
It was my fucking ass out there
on the line. Mine.

282
00:27:06,700 --> 00:27:10,100
This piddling shit
is the best that you come up with?

283
00:27:10,200 --> 00:27:12,700
You don't play me like that. You don't.

284
00:27:24,200 --> 00:27:28,600
Fuck you, you thieving, Greek cunt.

285
00:27:28,700 --> 00:27:29,900
Malaka!

286
00:27:37,900 --> 00:27:40,600
You don't know that one, chief.
But you know "malaka, " yes?

287
00:27:40,700 --> 00:27:43,000
Now you know malaka with dress.

288
00:28:57,900 --> 00:28:59,100
Please.

289
00:29:04,300 --> 00:29:05,400
Malaka.

290
00:29:15,500 --> 00:29:17,000
Can you hear me?

291
00:29:17,400 --> 00:29:19,700
If you can talk, please stay on the line.

292
00:30:55,500 --> 00:30:58,000
Get in the boat first,
then put the preserver on.

293
00:30:58,100 --> 00:31:00,300
-It's easier that way.
-Yeah?

294
00:31:01,000 --> 00:31:03,600
Y'all trying to drown my ass for sure.

295
00:31:07,600 --> 00:31:09,700
-Come on.
-Don't push me, man.

296
00:31:18,600 --> 00:31:19,900
Rod.

297
00:31:22,400 --> 00:31:23,400
Got it.

298
00:31:24,800 --> 00:31:27,300
Here. Hold on to that.

299
00:31:29,300 --> 00:31:31,100
I know this one.

300
00:31:45,800 --> 00:31:48,400
Stringer Bell will come at me with this.

301
00:31:49,000 --> 00:31:52,300
Says he's got something with Omar
he need to make straight.

302
00:31:53,200 --> 00:31:55,400
Didn't say what that might be?

303
00:31:55,900 --> 00:32:00,000
Wouldn't tell me.
And to be truthful, I didn't want to know.

304
00:32:05,400 --> 00:32:07,300
No. It don't feel right.

305
00:32:07,400 --> 00:32:10,300
You know them Barksdale people
ain't to be trusted.

306
00:32:10,400 --> 00:32:14,900
No denying all you say is true.
But Stringer talking parley.

307
00:32:15,500 --> 00:32:18,300
So your boy needs to think
long and hard on this.

308
00:32:18,400 --> 00:32:21,900
'Cause if Omar is living his day-to-day
in the street...

309
00:32:22,000 --> 00:32:26,000
there ain't no telling what their next step
might be if there ain't no sit-down.

310
00:32:26,100 --> 00:32:29,100
-"Parley"?
-That's all he says he's looking for.

311
00:32:33,300 --> 00:32:34,900
I'll talk to him.

312
00:32:36,400 --> 00:32:39,100
But if it feels funny to him
the way it does to me...

313
00:32:39,200 --> 00:32:42,800
I got a better chance
of putting a leash to the wind, you know?

314
00:32:43,200 --> 00:32:47,400
If you think it might help,
I can go protection.

315
00:32:48,000 --> 00:32:52,000
-They're the one got hurt the last time.
-Then there was a reason to meet.

316
00:32:53,800 --> 00:32:57,100
-This time feel different.
-I hear you.

317
00:32:58,000 --> 00:33:01,000
Maybe Stringer's still trying
to settle that beef...

318
00:33:01,100 --> 00:33:04,000
behind the fact
that he got to live in this city, too...

319
00:33:04,700 --> 00:33:06,900
Omar being Omar.

320
00:33:08,900 --> 00:33:11,400
If it ain't putting you out none...

321
00:33:11,500 --> 00:33:15,400
I'd feel a powerful lot better
if my nephew took over protection.

322
00:33:18,400 --> 00:33:19,700
Hayward.

323
00:33:30,600 --> 00:33:33,800
Typed and ready for your John Hancock.

324
00:33:42,500 --> 00:33:44,100
-Thanks.
-Sure.

325
00:34:02,900 --> 00:34:07,100
You just have to initial each page
and then sign at the end.

326
00:34:09,300 --> 00:34:13,200
I'm just checking.
This is the official record, right, chief?

327
00:34:15,000 --> 00:34:17,300
It's what's gonna play in court.

328
00:34:19,700 --> 00:34:21,800
Can I change something?

329
00:34:25,100 --> 00:34:26,100
Yeah.

330
00:34:31,300 --> 00:34:35,000
Just put your initials next to your changes.
It's no problem.

331
00:34:36,100 --> 00:34:37,600
Yeah, it's only one.

332
00:34:37,700 --> 00:34:42,100
-You know, you typed "said" here, see?
-"Said"?

333
00:34:50,100 --> 00:34:53,000
He wasn't saying, "Please don't shoot me."

334
00:34:54,800 --> 00:34:56,600
It was more begging.

335
00:34:59,300 --> 00:35:03,700
You know? Double G, he's begging me.

336
00:35:05,700 --> 00:35:08,400
But that's not gonna mess you up,
though, right?

337
00:35:11,400 --> 00:35:14,900
No, it's more descriptive like that.
It's good. Thanks.

338
00:35:40,900 --> 00:35:43,200
Quiet. No one in or out of there.

339
00:35:58,700 --> 00:36:02,000
It's kind of nice out here.
Moonlight on the water.

340
00:36:02,400 --> 00:36:05,700
Waves lapping gently against the boat.

341
00:36:09,900 --> 00:36:13,400
I'm working my regular eight.
I can handle it, you know?

342
00:36:13,900 --> 00:36:16,000
But a detail like this....

343
00:36:18,200 --> 00:36:20,000
That's what I'm asking.

344
00:36:20,100 --> 00:36:23,700
If something comes up on the job,
how would you handle it?

345
00:36:24,600 --> 00:36:26,800
I mean, at home with the kids.

346
00:36:27,900 --> 00:36:30,000
Until now, not much came up.

347
00:36:30,600 --> 00:36:33,500
But now, say something comes up.

348
00:36:34,300 --> 00:36:38,300
I mean, say we do a raid or something.
What would you do?

349
00:36:39,900 --> 00:36:42,700
I guess I'd try to get the sitter to stay.

350
00:36:42,800 --> 00:36:45,400
Maybe call my folks, like I did tonight.

351
00:36:46,100 --> 00:36:49,200
You know how it is with kids.
You gotta be there.

352
00:36:49,900 --> 00:36:51,500
But you wouldn't miss it?

353
00:36:51,600 --> 00:36:56,200
I mean, with everybody rolling out
and you having to head home?

354
00:36:58,800 --> 00:37:02,500
If it keeps going like this,
I don't know what I'm gonna do.

355
00:37:07,800 --> 00:37:09,900
-Thanks.
-It's no problem.

356
00:37:10,600 --> 00:37:13,000
You wanna make a phone call to someone?

357
00:37:13,400 --> 00:37:17,400
If you get over to Madison,
it might be some time before you can.

358
00:37:17,500 --> 00:37:20,000
Ain't a chance I get a bail, right?

359
00:37:26,000 --> 00:37:27,700
How about family?

360
00:37:39,500 --> 00:37:43,400
All right, to bring you up to speed,
we've got agents in Le Havre...

361
00:37:43,500 --> 00:37:47,400
shagging leads from the manifest
of the Talco ship due here in a few days.

362
00:37:47,600 --> 00:37:50,600
To see if we can't pinpoint the origin
for the illegal containers.

363
00:37:50,700 --> 00:37:52,400
That's a lot of cans.

364
00:37:52,600 --> 00:37:55,000
A hundred and ten, actually.

365
00:37:55,200 --> 00:37:59,300
How many agents you need to track back
to where all those cans came from?

366
00:37:59,400 --> 00:38:01,100
As many as it takes.

367
00:38:02,600 --> 00:38:07,200
We may be assholes, but on the upside,
there's an awful lot of us.

368
00:38:08,700 --> 00:38:12,200
Let me get this into the computer
for the boys overseas.

369
00:38:16,800 --> 00:38:19,400
Anything from that shithole of a diner?

370
00:38:19,900 --> 00:38:22,100
Herc and Carver had nothing overnight.

371
00:38:22,300 --> 00:38:25,400
The feds took over this morning
and it's still quiet.

372
00:38:25,500 --> 00:38:27,600
I'm going back on the water.

373
00:38:29,300 --> 00:38:31,400
One meet and we're on this guy.

374
00:39:09,600 --> 00:39:13,500
The Talco line's in Wednesday.
I'll send Nick for a number.

375
00:39:14,400 --> 00:39:16,700
-The Greeks again?
-Who else?

376
00:39:17,400 --> 00:39:20,200
They sure do stir up the shit,
them Greeks do.

377
00:39:22,900 --> 00:39:26,600
-Uncle Frank.
-Nicky boy, just in time.

378
00:39:26,700 --> 00:39:29,600
-Uncle Frank.
-What? What happened?

379
00:39:31,500 --> 00:39:34,300
-What the fuck is it this time?
-He shot....

380
00:39:35,600 --> 00:39:38,300
They're saying he shot two of the Greeks.

381
00:39:38,600 --> 00:39:41,000
-Last night, they're saying.
-Shot?

382
00:39:41,600 --> 00:39:44,100
-He shot?
-Fucking Christ!

383
00:39:44,200 --> 00:39:48,200
He's locked up.
He's fucking charged with murder.

384
00:39:48,300 --> 00:39:50,500
-The Greeks?
-Double G.

385
00:39:50,900 --> 00:39:54,300
And one of the kids that works
down the store on the avenue with him.

386
00:39:54,400 --> 00:39:56,600
They're saying he walked in there.

387
00:39:56,700 --> 00:39:59,000
-He went in.
-Why was he there?

388
00:39:59,300 --> 00:40:02,100
-Where the fuck were you?
-Uncle Frank, I didn't know.

389
00:40:02,200 --> 00:40:03,700
What didn't you know?

390
00:40:03,800 --> 00:40:07,100
-What is Ziggy doing near the Greeks?
-I don't know.

391
00:40:07,200 --> 00:40:10,200
You don't know? You're supposed to.
You're his fucking cousin!

392
00:40:10,200 --> 00:40:10,900
You don't know? You're supposed to.
You're his fucking cousin!

393
00:40:11,600 --> 00:40:13,200
You're his father.

394
00:40:23,900 --> 00:40:26,000
1,125 kilograms.

395
00:40:26,500 --> 00:40:28,800
Not that drug enforcement's my cup of tea...

396
00:40:28,900 --> 00:40:32,400
but I'm told
it was the largest crack seizure on record.

397
00:40:34,300 --> 00:40:36,600
I just wish I had good news for you.

398
00:40:38,500 --> 00:40:41,000
You told me this was a local effort.

399
00:40:41,100 --> 00:40:45,600
It's sprawled. Now the Bureau's involved.
We're looking hard at the port unions.

400
00:40:45,700 --> 00:40:47,300
My hands are tied.

401
00:40:50,800 --> 00:40:53,000
They're on you with wiretaps.

402
00:40:53,400 --> 00:40:55,800
Several phones, several addresses.

403
00:41:13,700 --> 00:41:15,000
Stefanos.

404
00:41:22,800 --> 00:41:24,700
Have the boy go to Eton.

405
00:41:24,800 --> 00:41:27,100
Tell him to come right away
to the other place.

406
00:41:27,200 --> 00:41:30,400
-You're not calling?
-No phones. No more phones.

407
00:41:33,100 --> 00:41:34,500
Adieu, my friend.

408
00:41:45,800 --> 00:41:47,600
They forgot your fries.

409
00:41:48,000 --> 00:41:50,100
No, they forgot your fries.

410
00:41:50,200 --> 00:41:53,500
-My fries are right in here.
-Those are my fries.

411
00:41:54,100 --> 00:41:58,100
Bitch, everything I say, you hear backwards.
The fries are mine, boy.

412
00:42:00,700 --> 00:42:02,000
Go ahead.

413
00:42:02,100 --> 00:42:05,100
Eat the fries, you fat fuck.
See if I fucking care.

414
00:42:05,200 --> 00:42:08,000
What? You think I'm fat?

415
00:42:16,200 --> 00:42:17,800
There's our boy.

416
00:42:20,200 --> 00:42:23,200
-Lester, Eton's on the move.
-We got it.

417
00:42:24,000 --> 00:42:27,500
-No need for an eyeball follow, right?
-No need.

418
00:42:28,000 --> 00:42:30,200
A fine fucking kettle of fish.

419
00:42:30,800 --> 00:42:34,000
I heard it,
but I had to come see it for myself.

420
00:42:34,300 --> 00:42:36,900
-And sure enough....
-Major?

421
00:42:37,900 --> 00:42:41,000
You know,
I put my faith in you fucking feds.

422
00:42:42,000 --> 00:42:43,600
You let me down.

423
00:42:44,000 --> 00:42:47,200
-Major, we can talk in my office.
-Lieutenant.

424
00:42:48,500 --> 00:42:50,300
It's Lieutenant, right?

425
00:42:50,800 --> 00:42:53,100
I gave you a simple assignment:

426
00:42:53,300 --> 00:42:56,300
that fellow, the one in the corner.

427
00:42:57,300 --> 00:43:00,200
And to make it happen, I gave you all this.

428
00:43:01,500 --> 00:43:03,900
Good digs, people...

429
00:43:04,600 --> 00:43:06,500
everything you needed.

430
00:43:07,000 --> 00:43:08,900
And what did you give me?

431
00:43:09,100 --> 00:43:12,600
Right up the fucking ass, Lieutenant.

432
00:43:13,000 --> 00:43:16,200
-Major, you're going to get--
-Roland, get your shit.

433
00:43:16,500 --> 00:43:18,600
You want to do it your way, fine.

434
00:43:18,800 --> 00:43:21,700
But you ain't gonna use my people
to fuck me.

435
00:43:24,800 --> 00:43:28,700
-Get your gear. I'm pulling you.
-I got.... There's work....

436
00:43:29,300 --> 00:43:32,600
-You said--
-Get your narrow ass back to the district...

437
00:43:32,700 --> 00:43:35,500
before I slap you with insubordination.

438
00:43:37,100 --> 00:43:38,800
Move, shitbird!

439
00:43:42,400 --> 00:43:43,700
Jesus!

440
00:44:04,200 --> 00:44:07,300
Detective, my office.

441
00:44:49,900 --> 00:44:53,300
Base to 11-34.
Target number two is coming at your 20.

442
00:44:53,600 --> 00:44:55,700
Copy that. We're on it good.

443
00:45:06,000 --> 00:45:07,700
We're on the Boss.

444
00:45:08,700 --> 00:45:09,900
My God.

445
00:45:10,900 --> 00:45:14,800
-He shoots both?
-He kills George, right there in the store.

446
00:45:15,400 --> 00:45:18,400
-Leaves the boy to bleed.
-For what?

447
00:45:20,400 --> 00:45:22,600
An argument over a few cars?

448
00:45:23,400 --> 00:45:26,100
-That little Polack?
-He's crazy, that one.

449
00:45:27,100 --> 00:45:29,000
The police have him now.

450
00:45:33,500 --> 00:45:35,300
The police still there?

451
00:45:37,200 --> 00:45:38,700
Go to the store.

452
00:45:39,500 --> 00:45:43,000
Whatever the police did not take,
papers, pictures, everything...

453
00:45:43,100 --> 00:45:44,800
you clean it up.

454
00:45:46,400 --> 00:45:49,400
The warehouse, too.
Everything gets clean now.

455
00:45:52,200 --> 00:45:53,600
Everything.

456
00:45:55,100 --> 00:45:57,100
And the phones are dead.

457
00:46:02,900 --> 00:46:05,800
Did you see that?
They just threw the phones.

458
00:46:07,400 --> 00:46:09,400
11-34 to Surveillance.

459
00:46:10,000 --> 00:46:12,300
-Standing by.
-We got our man.

460
00:46:12,400 --> 00:46:16,100
Target number one
is a white male, 40s, short...

461
00:46:16,200 --> 00:46:19,000
wearing a tan shirt and a gray tam.

462
00:46:19,800 --> 00:46:21,700
Copy your description.

463
00:46:23,000 --> 00:46:25,700
11-34 to Surveillance,
both targets are on the move.

464
00:46:25,800 --> 00:46:28,400
We can't make the vehicle from here,
but you sure can.

465
00:46:28,500 --> 00:46:29,500
Copy.

466
00:46:29,600 --> 00:46:32,200
What was he doing
with that thing in his hand?

467
00:46:33,100 --> 00:46:35,000
Same thing you always do.

468
00:46:35,500 --> 00:46:39,200
Probably sending a text message.
My kids are crazy over that.

469
00:46:55,700 --> 00:46:57,500
That's our guy, right?

470
00:46:58,200 --> 00:47:01,200
What's his face Sobotka
from the drug corner?

471
00:47:09,900 --> 00:47:11,900
I need to get with Vondas.

472
00:47:12,500 --> 00:47:13,900
Who's that?

473
00:47:19,400 --> 00:47:22,400
Spiros. Where is he?

474
00:47:23,500 --> 00:47:25,400
I don't know no Spiros.

475
00:47:42,600 --> 00:47:45,500
-No shit.
-He just up and clocked him?

476
00:47:45,600 --> 00:47:48,900
-Daniels had everybody write what they saw.
-Even us suits.

477
00:47:49,000 --> 00:47:51,100
That was smart. Daniels is sharp.

478
00:47:51,300 --> 00:47:53,900
-Where's Prez now?
-Daniels took him home.

479
00:47:54,000 --> 00:47:57,100
-I don't think he'll come back to this detail.
-You never know.

480
00:47:57,200 --> 00:48:00,700
He might have one of those psychological
bullshit things in his jacket...

481
00:48:00,800 --> 00:48:03,100
gives him immunity or something.

482
00:48:03,200 --> 00:48:07,000
Valchek gave him immunity,
and he just put Valchek on his ass.

483
00:48:10,900 --> 00:48:14,700
-Nothing since the Fort Howard meet.
-They're definitely dumping phones.

484
00:48:19,900 --> 00:48:24,000
When you use a cell phone and
press "send," where does the call go to?

485
00:48:24,100 --> 00:48:26,800
-Why are you asking?
-The Boss Man at Fort Howard.

486
00:48:26,900 --> 00:48:29,200
He tosses the cell phone we're up on, right?

487
00:48:29,300 --> 00:48:33,100
Then he pulls out another thingamajig,
and he types a message.

488
00:48:33,200 --> 00:48:34,700
Text messaging.

489
00:48:36,200 --> 00:48:40,000
It starts at one of those towers
they got up all over the place, right?

490
00:48:40,100 --> 00:48:42,800
And ends up in a computer
at a wireless provider.

491
00:48:42,900 --> 00:48:47,200
If you knew when the call was made,
could you trace the call back to that tower?

492
00:48:47,500 --> 00:48:49,900
'Cause if you could,
mightn't you get a phone number?

493
00:48:50,000 --> 00:48:52,500
You get that,
then you got the billing details, right?

494
00:48:52,600 --> 00:48:55,700
Fool, do you have any idea
how many people use cell phones?

495
00:48:55,800 --> 00:48:59,300
There must be thousands,
hundreds of thousands at any time.

496
00:48:59,400 --> 00:49:01,700
What you need is another variable.

497
00:49:01,800 --> 00:49:06,000
Another bit of data that's gonna help you
isolate your call from all the others.

498
00:49:06,100 --> 00:49:10,300
What if you knew where the call was made?
I mean, exactly where it was made.

499
00:49:11,100 --> 00:49:14,900
We were out in the middle of nowhere.
Does that help narrow it down?

500
00:49:15,000 --> 00:49:19,300
The Fort Howard sea wall. It ain't exactly
Charles and Baltimore Streets.

501
00:49:19,400 --> 00:49:22,600
You've got another problem.
Which wireless company?

502
00:49:22,700 --> 00:49:26,800
There must be Verizon, MCI, AT&T, Sprint....

503
00:49:27,200 --> 00:49:30,100
Shit, tin cans and a string.
You got dozens of them.

504
00:49:38,500 --> 00:49:39,900
Lamar?

505
00:49:40,900 --> 00:49:43,200
-Where's my Harper's?
-Say what?

506
00:49:43,300 --> 00:49:44,900
Harper's. The new issue.

507
00:49:45,000 --> 00:49:48,100
You didn't say that one.
You said The New Republic and Atlantic...

508
00:49:48,200 --> 00:49:51,300
-and a new something else.
-I did not forget to tell you Harper's.

509
00:49:51,400 --> 00:49:55,900
Every week I tell you the same shit,
and every week you forget half of what I say.

510
00:49:56,000 --> 00:49:59,600
Tomorrow, first thing, you go
to the newsstand and you get Harper's.

511
00:49:59,700 --> 00:50:03,200
And The Nation, too,
which you also managed to forget.

512
00:50:05,000 --> 00:50:08,400
You know what the most dangerous thing
in America is, right?

513
00:50:10,500 --> 00:50:12,600
A nigger with a library card.

514
00:50:15,100 --> 00:50:18,600
All damn day, he just sit there reading.

515
00:50:19,900 --> 00:50:22,700
And damned if them Eastside bitches
don't stay away.

516
00:50:22,800 --> 00:50:25,600
-That's real muscle, right there.
-True that.

517
00:50:26,800 --> 00:50:30,300
What are we gonna do
when we start running out of good product?

518
00:50:30,600 --> 00:50:32,700
That's what we need to ask ourselves.

519
00:50:32,800 --> 00:50:36,300
Yo, Bodie,
if Stringer want the Eastside up in here...

520
00:50:36,700 --> 00:50:39,600
then why Barksdale got a man
running them off?

521
00:50:50,000 --> 00:50:53,800
This is getting us nowhere.
We got nothing under Pyramid lnc...

522
00:50:53,900 --> 00:50:56,500
or any of the targets
at any other cellular company.

523
00:50:56,600 --> 00:50:58,100
It's on McNulty then.

524
00:50:58,900 --> 00:51:01,000
11-35, you got the 20?

525
00:51:01,100 --> 00:51:04,000
-I'm on the spot right now.
-Go.

526
00:51:04,700 --> 00:51:09,100
10-4. Latitude first:
North, 39 degrees, 11.727.

527
00:51:09,500 --> 00:51:13,700
Longitude: West, 76 degrees. 26.628.

528
00:51:16,500 --> 00:51:20,100
Now, this was a neat trick.
No one ever did it before.

529
00:51:20,600 --> 00:51:23,300
Identified a cell phone using time and GPS.

530
00:51:23,400 --> 00:51:26,200
We got everything on the phone
that was text messaging...

531
00:51:26,300 --> 00:51:29,200
from those coordinates at 04:45 p.m. today.

532
00:51:34,800 --> 00:51:36,200
Just a subpoena?

533
00:51:36,300 --> 00:51:40,000
With this, you can get account information
and a phone number.

534
00:51:40,100 --> 00:51:41,700
With a search warrant...

535
00:51:41,800 --> 00:51:45,400
you can get two months of text messages.

536
00:51:46,300 --> 00:51:49,100
You got two months of text messages
in this file?

537
00:51:49,200 --> 00:51:51,300
I do, if you've got a warrant.

538
00:51:53,100 --> 00:51:54,600
Tell you what, friend.

539
00:51:54,700 --> 00:51:57,900
We're gonna go back and
start typing that warrant tomorrow morning.

540
00:51:58,000 --> 00:52:00,400
But right now,
we wouldn't mind taking a peek...

541
00:52:00,500 --> 00:52:02,900
at what my man's been up to
in the last 24 hours.

542
00:52:03,000 --> 00:52:04,800
Exigent circumstances.

543
00:52:09,100 --> 00:52:10,700
Thanks, brother.

544
00:52:15,800 --> 00:52:17,000
Fuck me.

545
00:52:19,600 --> 00:52:21,200
Nothing's easy.

546
00:52:24,500 --> 00:52:27,600
-What's up?
-They've dumped their phones.

547
00:52:28,400 --> 00:52:31,500
We're trying to get onto
the Boss Man's text messaging.

548
00:52:33,100 --> 00:52:35,400
They sent that Greek mess over as email.

549
00:52:35,500 --> 00:52:38,100
After he inputs,
the computer will translate it.

550
00:52:38,200 --> 00:52:39,200
Got it.

551
00:52:42,400 --> 00:52:43,700
Shit.

552
00:52:58,000 --> 00:52:59,500
Hey, Prissy.

553
00:53:01,200 --> 00:53:03,100
Thought you'd be here.

554
00:53:27,500 --> 00:53:29,000
Fucking Ziggy.

555
00:53:29,900 --> 00:53:32,000
When didn't he do dumb shit?

556
00:53:33,200 --> 00:53:36,300
Remember when he forged
that Age of Majority card?

557
00:53:38,800 --> 00:53:40,700
We all pooled our money.

558
00:53:41,000 --> 00:53:43,600
You drove us over Brooklyn Park
to the cut-rate.

559
00:53:43,700 --> 00:53:45,800
My mom's puke-yellow Chevy.

560
00:53:46,900 --> 00:53:48,900
We told him specifically:

561
00:53:49,100 --> 00:53:51,500
two bottles of Pikesville Rye and....

562
00:53:54,200 --> 00:53:56,200
Southern Comfort for me.

563
00:54:01,300 --> 00:54:03,100
What did fucknuts get?

564
00:54:05,100 --> 00:54:07,000
Fucking Boone's Farm.

565
00:54:11,700 --> 00:54:14,500
He said that's what the college kids drank.

566
00:54:15,200 --> 00:54:18,000
But we did it up. Right here.

567
00:54:24,600 --> 00:54:28,000
He stood up there, a bottle in each hand...

568
00:54:29,500 --> 00:54:32,200
screaming loud enough to wake the nuns.

569
00:54:34,500 --> 00:54:36,400
What the fuck did he say?

570
00:54:48,300 --> 00:54:51,000
"College kids ain't shit!"

571
00:55:17,900 --> 00:55:19,400
Goddamn, Zig.

572
00:55:38,600 --> 00:55:41,200
-Yeah?
-Beadie, it's Kima.

573
00:55:42,600 --> 00:55:44,600
We're gonna take the Boss out.

574
00:55:44,700 --> 00:55:48,700
-Raids? Tonight?
-You got somewhere to drop the kids off?

575
00:55:48,800 --> 00:55:52,300
No, no problem.
I can take them over to my parents'.

576
00:55:53,700 --> 00:55:55,700
All right, we'll see you soon.

577
00:55:55,800 --> 00:55:59,000
Kima, thanks for the call. Bye.

578
00:56:11,000 --> 00:56:13,600
The judge wants to know how much longer.

579
00:56:13,700 --> 00:56:14,900
We're close.

580
00:56:22,500 --> 00:56:25,800
Dump this row. Dump the computer.
Dump this.



## S02E11

1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:04,162
WWW.MY-SUBS.CO

1
00:00:23,100 --> 00:00:25,600
Wake up, Baltimore. It's 6:00 a.m....

2
00:00:25,700 --> 00:00:26,900
Police!

3
00:00:41,400 --> 00:00:42,500
Ready?

4
00:00:43,900 --> 00:00:45,300
Freeze, FBl!

5
00:00:49,000 --> 00:00:51,100
-All clear.
-Check upstairs.

6
00:00:53,400 --> 00:00:55,000
Turn around.

7
00:00:55,400 --> 00:00:57,900
Put your hands up. Behind your neck.

8
00:00:59,300 --> 00:01:00,900
Keep them there.

9
00:01:18,500 --> 00:01:20,600
No, nothing here. All clear.

10
00:01:53,500 --> 00:01:54,700
All clear.

11
00:02:05,100 --> 00:02:08,000
You won't find a goddamn thing!
I can tell you that right now.

12
00:02:08,100 --> 00:02:09,900
Ain't got shit on me.

13
00:02:13,400 --> 00:02:16,500
Fuck! You ain't got nothing.
I'm telling you. Nothing!

14
00:02:23,500 --> 00:02:25,000
Move, shitbird.

15
00:02:37,300 --> 00:02:39,200
FBl, show me your hands!

16
00:02:47,200 --> 00:02:49,100
Get down, fuck! Get down!

17
00:03:03,500 --> 00:03:04,500
Nice.

18
00:03:18,600 --> 00:03:19,700
Bingo.

19
00:03:23,600 --> 00:03:27,500
-From behind your clothes washer.
-That's heroin, 300 gelcaps.

20
00:03:37,000 --> 00:03:38,900
And on today's Chip Franklin Show
at noon...

21
00:03:39,000 --> 00:03:42,500
Chip will be live at Arundel Mills Mall
asking local retailers:

22
00:03:42,600 --> 00:03:44,900
"What do you get
for the guy who has everything?"

23
00:03:45,000 --> 00:03:47,000
Now here's Steve Stewart with sports.

24
00:03:47,100 --> 00:03:48,500
The Orioles continue to....

25
00:05:47,300 --> 00:05:50,600
-We could take him now.
-Not enough profile.

26
00:05:53,000 --> 00:05:54,400
Fucking feds.

27
00:05:55,000 --> 00:05:57,600
Be advised, target 27 is on the move.

28
00:06:09,800 --> 00:06:13,100
I don't get it.
Why leave Vondopoulos out on the street?

29
00:06:13,500 --> 00:06:17,100
The text message that told him to clean up,
it came from someone higher up.

30
00:06:17,200 --> 00:06:18,500
Someone we don't know.

31
00:06:18,600 --> 00:06:20,700
We leave him on the street
after these raids...

32
00:06:20,800 --> 00:06:23,300
he'll probably make contact
with whoever's above him.

33
00:06:23,400 --> 00:06:26,000
Either another text message or a meet.

34
00:06:26,700 --> 00:06:28,200
What's with George Glekas?

35
00:06:28,300 --> 00:06:31,100
I'm afraid he's gonna duck this warrant.

36
00:06:32,500 --> 00:06:36,200
-Chester Karol Sobotka?
-It's Frank Sobotka's kid.

37
00:06:36,400 --> 00:06:39,600
Frank's kid kills one of our targets?
Are you shitting me?

38
00:06:39,700 --> 00:06:41,100
Why? What for?

39
00:06:41,700 --> 00:06:43,200
We hit the store this morning.

40
00:06:43,300 --> 00:06:46,300
Every shred of paper's gone.
Just a bloodstain on the floor.

41
00:06:46,400 --> 00:06:49,500
So we go over to his house a half hour later
with the warrant...

42
00:06:49,600 --> 00:06:54,100
and it's full up with red-eyed Greek relations
looking at us like we're braindeads.

43
00:06:57,300 --> 00:06:58,700
Homicide, Shea.

44
00:06:58,800 --> 00:07:01,400
-This is Daniels, out at Southeast.
-Yes, sir.

45
00:07:01,500 --> 00:07:04,300
Who caught the Highlandtown murder
the night before last?

46
00:07:04,400 --> 00:07:06,100
Jay Landsman, sir.

47
00:07:08,100 --> 00:07:09,800
I'll be right over.

48
00:07:17,000 --> 00:07:19,200
Go get the interviews started.

49
00:07:34,700 --> 00:07:36,400
-Lieutenant?
-Hey, Lt.

50
00:07:45,200 --> 00:07:47,300
What the fuck is that about?

51
00:07:48,600 --> 00:07:50,600
How did we do this morning?

52
00:07:50,800 --> 00:07:53,700
Eton and Sergei are in. So is the madam.

53
00:07:53,900 --> 00:07:55,700
Glekas, I'm not sure.

54
00:07:57,600 --> 00:08:01,400
-The feds are waiting on Sobotka.
-What are they waiting for?

55
00:08:02,200 --> 00:08:03,700
You don't wanna know.

56
00:08:04,000 --> 00:08:04,300
Jesus, Larry....

57
00:08:04,300 --> 00:08:05,300
Jesus, Larry....

58
00:08:05,400 --> 00:08:08,900
The thing is, I think we gotta reach out
to a criminal lawyer real quick.

59
00:08:09,000 --> 00:08:11,100
If the union guys can't handle this mess...

60
00:08:11,200 --> 00:08:13,100
he's gonna have a bail hearing tomorrow.

61
00:08:13,200 --> 00:08:15,800
-Do you have any details?
-I don't know nothing...

62
00:08:15,900 --> 00:08:18,500
except he's locked up for it.
I can't see him till 10:00.

63
00:08:18,600 --> 00:08:21,400
-That's the only time?
-Visiting hours, yeah.

64
00:08:21,500 --> 00:08:23,500
Look, everything's gonna be fine.

65
00:08:34,000 --> 00:08:37,000
-FBI! All of you move, now!
-What the fuck is this?

66
00:08:37,800 --> 00:08:40,000
-FBI, move!
-Against the wall.

67
00:08:42,600 --> 00:08:44,200
He's here.

68
00:08:48,200 --> 00:08:50,500
Got another problem here, Larry.

69
00:09:00,900 --> 00:09:02,700
Big man on the docks.

70
00:09:04,200 --> 00:09:06,600
You don't look so big now, do you?

71
00:09:49,200 --> 00:09:50,200
Ma.

72
00:10:12,500 --> 00:10:13,500
Pop.

73
00:10:28,100 --> 00:10:29,400
It's gone.

74
00:10:30,700 --> 00:10:32,400
And the money, too.

75
00:10:34,300 --> 00:10:36,400
They say you need to come in.

76
00:10:36,800 --> 00:10:40,400
They said the warrant
is at Southeastern police district.

77
00:10:46,400 --> 00:10:48,300
They're out there now.

78
00:10:50,000 --> 00:10:51,600
Showtime, Franky.

79
00:11:04,200 --> 00:11:06,200
-Frank.
-Sir, any comment?

80
00:11:06,900 --> 00:11:09,000
Is it just you, or is it the whole union?

81
00:11:09,100 --> 00:11:12,400
What's your comment
on the charges being brought against you?

82
00:11:13,700 --> 00:11:17,100
Sir, do you have anything at all to say?
Any comment at all?

83
00:11:17,200 --> 00:11:20,000
How will you answer
the charges against you?

84
00:11:21,700 --> 00:11:25,300
Let me ask you, who exactly am I working
all these dead girls for?

85
00:11:25,400 --> 00:11:26,800
The Homicide unit, right?

86
00:11:26,900 --> 00:11:30,800
The same Homicide unit that can't put
two and two together and pick up a phone...

87
00:11:30,900 --> 00:11:34,600
leaving me to read it a day-and-a-half later
in The Baltimore Sun.

88
00:11:40,400 --> 00:11:44,800
-What did you take from the scene?
-Photos, latents, spent casings.

89
00:11:48,300 --> 00:11:49,300
Fuck.

90
00:11:49,700 --> 00:11:51,900
They cleaned everything else?

91
00:11:53,700 --> 00:11:56,700
Even for a supremely
fucked-up police department...

92
00:11:56,800 --> 00:11:58,600
this takes the prize.

93
00:12:05,900 --> 00:12:07,800
How'd the kid play it?

94
00:12:07,900 --> 00:12:09,500
He signed a full statement.

95
00:12:09,600 --> 00:12:13,000
He said that there was an argument
about a stolen car or two.

96
00:12:13,100 --> 00:12:15,000
Think he'll open up and talk more?

97
00:12:15,200 --> 00:12:17,200
He's been processed and assigned a PD.

98
00:12:17,300 --> 00:12:21,600
If you want to take a run at the kid,
you're gonna have to get around his lawyer.

99
00:12:23,200 --> 00:12:26,500
I'm sorry, Lieutenant. It's my bad.

100
00:12:32,000 --> 00:12:34,800
State your name, asshole.
What's your name?

101
00:12:36,200 --> 00:12:37,800
What's your name?

102
00:12:48,500 --> 00:12:50,000
State your name.

103
00:12:52,200 --> 00:12:55,100
Come on, you know this part.
Give us a name.

104
00:12:59,600 --> 00:13:01,300
There is your name.

105
00:13:03,600 --> 00:13:05,200
State your name.

106
00:13:09,100 --> 00:13:10,300
No name?

107
00:13:12,000 --> 00:13:15,100
-For now, we'll just call you Boris.
-Boris.

108
00:13:17,200 --> 00:13:18,900
Why always "Boris"?

109
00:13:19,800 --> 00:13:23,700
Racketeering. Wire fraud.
Conspiracy to import heroin.

110
00:13:23,800 --> 00:13:26,900
Conspiracy to violate
federal customs statutes.

111
00:13:27,000 --> 00:13:28,500
White slavery.

112
00:13:29,800 --> 00:13:33,600
Today we're only charging
the customs violations, Mr. Sobotka.

113
00:13:34,200 --> 00:13:38,100
But eventually, a grand jury indictment
will expose you to a lot more.

114
00:13:38,100 --> 00:13:38,500
But eventually, a grand jury indictment
will expose you to a lot more.

115
00:13:40,900 --> 00:13:45,200
Name names, and come clean.
You help yourself and your union.

116
00:13:46,100 --> 00:13:47,600
Help my union?

117
00:13:51,000 --> 00:13:53,900
For 25 years,
we've been dying slow down there.

118
00:13:55,300 --> 00:13:58,200
Dry docks rusting, piers standing empty.

119
00:13:59,700 --> 00:14:02,400
My friends and their kids,
like we got the cancer.

120
00:14:02,500 --> 00:14:06,200
No lifeline got thrown all that time.
Nothing from nobody.

121
00:14:07,700 --> 00:14:09,700
And now you wanna help us?

122
00:14:10,800 --> 00:14:12,000
Help me?

123
00:14:18,400 --> 00:14:21,000
-What's your full name?
-Michael McArdle.

124
00:14:21,100 --> 00:14:22,800
-White Mike.
-Yeah, that's right.

125
00:14:22,900 --> 00:14:24,200
Listen to this, Mikey.

126
00:14:24,300 --> 00:14:25,900
I wanna know it wasn't your people...

127
00:14:26,000 --> 00:14:28,200
dropped that body on Potee Street
the other night.

128
00:14:28,300 --> 00:14:30,800
I'm asking 'cause it was someone
with a Greek-ass name...

129
00:14:31,000 --> 00:14:33,700
and fuck if he wasn't dumped
in front of a house I was using.

130
00:14:33,800 --> 00:14:36,300
Did he have hands? Did he have a face?

131
00:14:36,400 --> 00:14:38,300
Yes? Then it wasn't us.

132
00:14:41,400 --> 00:14:43,100
We hit your suppliers.

133
00:14:43,200 --> 00:14:45,400
They cleaned up
and left you holding the dirt.

134
00:14:45,500 --> 00:14:48,500
-Suppliers of what?
-You discussed a drug buy on this tape.

135
00:14:48,600 --> 00:14:51,400
We also have photographs
tying you to your stash house...

136
00:14:51,500 --> 00:14:55,500
and putting you at The Greek's warehouse
over on Newkirk Street for re-ups.

137
00:14:57,100 --> 00:14:59,400
Do yourself a solid here, Mike.

138
00:15:11,700 --> 00:15:14,600
-What's the plan?
-This is just a detention hearing, Frank.

139
00:15:14,700 --> 00:15:17,400
You're not a flight risk,
you have no meaningful priors.

140
00:15:17,500 --> 00:15:19,900
And so far they've only hit you
with one count.

141
00:15:20,000 --> 00:15:22,900
The magistrate's gonna ask us
some basic questions.

142
00:15:23,000 --> 00:15:25,500
Barring anything unforeseen,
you're out in an hour.

143
00:15:25,600 --> 00:15:28,200
-I said nothing to them suits.
-All the better.

144
00:15:29,600 --> 00:15:33,100
-This Eton, he's in charge of what exactly?
-The dope.

145
00:15:34,000 --> 00:15:35,600
He's what, Greek?

146
00:15:35,800 --> 00:15:39,100
He's a Jew.
You know, from that Jew country they got.

147
00:15:39,200 --> 00:15:43,400
-And what about the guy they call Sergei?
-Sergei's straight muscle.

148
00:15:44,200 --> 00:15:47,700
-Look, I need something to eat.
-Okay, what do you want?

149
00:15:48,300 --> 00:15:50,800
Two hot dogs and a strawberry soda.

150
00:15:51,800 --> 00:15:53,700
I'd fuck the order up.

151
00:15:55,900 --> 00:15:57,900
It's gotta be strawberry?

152
00:15:58,400 --> 00:15:59,800
Hook a brother up.

153
00:16:07,600 --> 00:16:10,500
Big man, that ain't gonna work for Omar.

154
00:16:12,100 --> 00:16:13,600
It's all right.

155
00:16:19,300 --> 00:16:20,900
Been what, a year?

156
00:16:22,400 --> 00:16:25,400
Boy, you don't know,
I been dreaming of running into you again.

157
00:16:25,500 --> 00:16:28,100
You got a focus. I give you that.

158
00:16:28,300 --> 00:16:31,200
Man be like that when he got work to do.
You know what I mean?

159
00:16:31,300 --> 00:16:32,900
I think you've done enough.

160
00:16:33,000 --> 00:16:35,900
Bird gone.
Wee-Bey copped out to all them murders.

161
00:16:36,000 --> 00:16:38,400
He in jail now forever and a day.

162
00:16:38,600 --> 00:16:42,700
Stinkum? I mean, you closed the book
on that nigger your damn self.

163
00:16:42,800 --> 00:16:46,500
Avon, he out of pocket for the time being.

164
00:16:47,300 --> 00:16:48,600
Leaving you.

165
00:16:48,700 --> 00:16:52,200
-You looking for closure?
-Lookit, man, ain't no closure.

166
00:16:53,200 --> 00:16:57,200
Not unless Brandon walk up out his grave
and come up in this room right now.

167
00:16:57,300 --> 00:17:01,000
See, all I know is whoever did him that way,
they gets got.

168
00:17:01,700 --> 00:17:05,300
Whoever did him that way,
they still out there right now.

169
00:17:05,500 --> 00:17:08,100
So now you gonna play like
you had nothing to do with it.

170
00:17:08,200 --> 00:17:09,700
No, I can't lie.

171
00:17:09,800 --> 00:17:14,200
I put the motherfucking paper out on y'all.
But y'all was fucking with my stash.

172
00:17:14,500 --> 00:17:17,100
Anything after that, part of the game.

173
00:17:17,400 --> 00:17:20,600
Maybe. But see,
I went past that with Brandon.

174
00:17:22,000 --> 00:17:24,800
That wasn't me. That wasn't Avon, either.

175
00:17:25,200 --> 00:17:29,600
Bird and them were there to see it.
But another man did all the extras:

176
00:17:30,900 --> 00:17:32,900
all that cigarette shit...

177
00:17:33,600 --> 00:17:35,600
all that bullshit with the eyes.

178
00:17:35,700 --> 00:17:39,100
See now, this man,
he building a rep for himself...

179
00:17:39,500 --> 00:17:41,300
and he wants you bad.

180
00:17:41,600 --> 00:17:44,700
The brutal shit, that's his calling card.

181
00:17:46,000 --> 00:17:49,000
Little bow-tie wearing motherfucker
from out of....

182
00:17:49,100 --> 00:17:50,100
NYC?

183
00:17:50,900 --> 00:17:52,500
Yeah, small dude.

184
00:17:55,300 --> 00:17:56,800
What he go by?

185
00:17:58,300 --> 00:17:59,800
Brother Mouzone.

186
00:18:02,200 --> 00:18:04,500
I know you heard of him, right?

187
00:18:05,900 --> 00:18:08,100
So if y'all got the mind to go after him...

188
00:18:08,200 --> 00:18:11,300
I might be able to point you
in that direction.

189
00:18:11,800 --> 00:18:12,800
Why?

190
00:18:13,700 --> 00:18:16,200
What happened to your boy was business.

191
00:18:16,600 --> 00:18:20,500
But how that shit happened,
you got the right to take that to heart.

192
00:18:20,600 --> 00:18:22,800
I figure that'll make us even.

193
00:18:23,400 --> 00:18:26,100
Now, you wanna know where this nigger is?

194
00:18:28,900 --> 00:18:32,100
-We need to sit down and talk, Frank.
-I gotta see my son.

195
00:18:32,200 --> 00:18:34,900
The man's right.
Let's grab a cup of coffee or something.

196
00:18:35,000 --> 00:18:37,200
Not now, I need to get clean.

197
00:18:40,000 --> 00:18:41,600
Sergei and them...

198
00:18:43,900 --> 00:18:45,600
they did Mau Mau Willis.

199
00:18:45,700 --> 00:18:48,600
-Why'd they chill him?
-He was welshing on the Jew.

200
00:18:48,700 --> 00:18:53,000
Okay, Sergei's a soldier.
But he and Eton report to somebody.

201
00:18:53,700 --> 00:18:56,600
-Who's above those two, Mike?
-I don't know.

202
00:18:58,700 --> 00:19:01,200
-You don't know?
-Never did wanna know.

203
00:19:12,900 --> 00:19:15,700
God in heaven, Zig,
the cops do that to you?

204
00:19:17,300 --> 00:19:18,700
Ain't the cops.

205
00:19:29,600 --> 00:19:32,500
Lawyers are saying the bail might be tough.

206
00:19:34,000 --> 00:19:35,400
I'm trying.

207
00:19:36,800 --> 00:19:38,900
You know I'm trying, right?

208
00:19:41,500 --> 00:19:44,200
-What happened?
-I don't know.

209
00:19:46,100 --> 00:19:47,500
I got tired.

210
00:19:50,900 --> 00:19:54,100
I got tired of being the punchline
to every joke.

211
00:19:59,400 --> 00:20:02,000
You had problems,
you could've come to me.

212
00:20:02,200 --> 00:20:04,300
You could've said something.

213
00:20:05,600 --> 00:20:07,500
You wouldn't have heard.

214
00:20:08,800 --> 00:20:11,800
You were always too busy
dredging up the canal.

215
00:20:13,200 --> 00:20:15,800
Making sure the right bum got elected.

216
00:20:16,800 --> 00:20:19,300
Buying another round for the house.

217
00:20:25,400 --> 00:20:29,600
I always used to think you were working
all them hours you spent away.

218
00:20:30,100 --> 00:20:33,600
It was all work, Zig, even when it wasn't.

219
00:20:34,700 --> 00:20:36,900
For you, for your mother.

220
00:20:38,300 --> 00:20:41,300
I bet you didn't even tell her
I was in here, did you?

221
00:20:41,900 --> 00:20:43,400
Maybe you did...

222
00:20:43,700 --> 00:20:47,700
and she already took three Nembutals,
sleeping the day away.

223
00:20:48,600 --> 00:20:52,200
-Leave her out of this.
-She's out of it, don't worry.

224
00:20:57,300 --> 00:20:58,300
Pop...

225
00:21:01,900 --> 00:21:05,000
when I seen what I did
to that kid down at the store...

226
00:21:05,100 --> 00:21:07,300
it made me sick to my stomach.

227
00:21:09,700 --> 00:21:12,100
-That ain't you, Zig.
-It ain't?

228
00:21:14,100 --> 00:21:17,300
Because the same blood
don't flow for us, Pop.

229
00:21:17,400 --> 00:21:20,000
I mean, I wish it did, but it don't.

230
00:21:21,300 --> 00:21:23,700
You're more like me than you know.

231
00:21:27,700 --> 00:21:29,300
You're a Sobotka.

232
00:21:34,400 --> 00:21:36,900
Fucked is what I am.

233
00:21:51,600 --> 00:21:53,400
What the fuck can I say?

234
00:22:19,000 --> 00:22:21,900
Best progress so far
is "White Mike" McArdle.

235
00:22:22,000 --> 00:22:23,700
He's standing on the edge of the cliff.

236
00:22:23,800 --> 00:22:27,800
We're gonna get Pearlman in today
to see what she can do to step him off.

237
00:22:27,900 --> 00:22:30,800
Also, we're still hunting
the Sobotka nephew.

238
00:22:31,000 --> 00:22:32,600
Herc and Carver are on that.

239
00:22:32,700 --> 00:22:35,600
Still, my guess is the drug players...

240
00:22:36,800 --> 00:22:39,700
even if they roll, give us Eton and Sergei.

241
00:22:40,500 --> 00:22:43,400
The case gets thin when we get up to this...

242
00:22:45,200 --> 00:22:46,800
Spiros Vondopoulos.

243
00:22:46,900 --> 00:22:49,300
Boy, them Greeks
and those twisted-ass names.

244
00:22:49,400 --> 00:22:51,800
Lay off the Greeks.
They invented civilization.

245
00:22:51,900 --> 00:22:53,700
Yeah? Ass-fucking, too.

246
00:22:54,100 --> 00:22:56,600
What exactly do we know
about Vondopoulos?

247
00:22:56,700 --> 00:22:59,600
We should stay on him, see who he really is.

248
00:22:59,800 --> 00:23:01,200
How about it?

249
00:23:01,500 --> 00:23:04,700
Throw us a few
of your well-equipped surveillance teams?

250
00:23:05,100 --> 00:23:08,700
In case you haven't noticed, Lieutenant,
I'm the only fed still in the room.

251
00:23:08,800 --> 00:23:11,600
The US attorney has what he wants
with the union guys...

252
00:23:11,700 --> 00:23:15,300
which means my field office
is pretty much over this case.

253
00:23:15,500 --> 00:23:18,300
Okay, we're on Vondopoulos ourselves.

254
00:23:22,700 --> 00:23:24,400
I'm sorry for him...

255
00:23:25,600 --> 00:23:27,000
and for you.

256
00:23:28,800 --> 00:23:31,700
We should've paid more attention
to our own.

257
00:23:32,000 --> 00:23:35,200
Like I could've stopped Ziggy
from what he'd done.

258
00:23:35,800 --> 00:23:37,900
Like anyone could ever control him.

259
00:23:38,000 --> 00:23:40,200
I was thinking of my boy, too.

260
00:23:42,800 --> 00:23:44,900
They're dropping the net on all the guys.

261
00:23:45,000 --> 00:23:47,900
Ain't no secret
things get lost in them cans now and again.

262
00:23:48,000 --> 00:23:49,700
He'll be all right.

263
00:23:50,300 --> 00:23:52,500
They tossed my house, Frank.

264
00:23:53,200 --> 00:23:56,800
They don't do that when there's
a couple of cases of vodka missing.

265
00:23:59,000 --> 00:24:03,800
They made me sign the search warrant.
That's a receipt-like for what they found.

266
00:24:04,900 --> 00:24:08,000
Heroin, Frank. From this house.

267
00:24:08,500 --> 00:24:11,600
No, that ain't right. That can't be right.

268
00:24:13,000 --> 00:24:17,500
I knew Nicky and Zig was boosting stuff.
Cameras, shit like that. Nothing like this.

269
00:24:17,600 --> 00:24:18,800
You knew?

270
00:24:20,600 --> 00:24:24,100
And once Nicky got used to boosting stuff
and seeing a little money...

271
00:24:24,200 --> 00:24:28,500
what did you think he was gonna do?
Turn straight all of a sudden and give it up?

272
00:24:28,800 --> 00:24:30,300
No, Frank.

273
00:24:31,000 --> 00:24:34,200
Once you gave him
a taste on the house, just....

274
00:24:34,700 --> 00:24:38,500
That was never.... I mean, he knew. He knew.

275
00:24:39,100 --> 00:24:41,300
Everything I did, the cans I let through...

276
00:24:41,400 --> 00:24:44,000
the money we got from that
went to keeping what we had.

277
00:24:44,100 --> 00:24:45,800
God damn it, Frank!

278
00:24:47,600 --> 00:24:51,100
Don't let that excuse this. Not this.

279
00:24:54,800 --> 00:24:57,400
Uncle Frank, with the big shoulders.

280
00:24:58,200 --> 00:25:00,700
"If it's broke, give it to my uncle.

281
00:25:01,700 --> 00:25:03,300
"He can fix it."

282
00:25:28,400 --> 00:25:31,400
Hey, Killer.
I got something for you, come here.

283
00:25:47,200 --> 00:25:49,400
You got the new Harper's yet?

284
00:25:51,100 --> 00:25:53,000
Now, you know stores down the way...

285
00:25:53,100 --> 00:25:56,000
don't have nothing past Vibe
and Handguns Today.

286
00:25:56,400 --> 00:25:58,800
Some titty mags, too, if you need.

287
00:25:59,000 --> 00:26:01,100
All right. I got you.

288
00:26:01,500 --> 00:26:04,200
I'm gonna hook you up, though, all right?

289
00:26:09,000 --> 00:26:11,900
Hey, boy. Told you I had something for you.

290
00:26:12,100 --> 00:26:13,600
There you go.

291
00:26:14,400 --> 00:26:16,100
That's my good boy.

292
00:27:07,000 --> 00:27:08,700
Good day for a ship.

293
00:27:09,400 --> 00:27:12,900
This is the hiring hall, Frank.
Working stevedores only.

294
00:27:17,100 --> 00:27:19,400
Big Roy, let me have your card.

295
00:27:21,400 --> 00:27:22,900
What do you want my card for?

296
00:27:23,000 --> 00:27:25,700
Not you. Little Big Roy,
let me hold your card.

297
00:27:26,000 --> 00:27:28,900
I need it.
I'm gonna work the Cape St. George today.

298
00:27:29,000 --> 00:27:31,600
-I'll work it for you.
-Work it for me?

299
00:27:31,800 --> 00:27:35,400
I work the ship on your card.
You work a barstool down Clement Street.

300
00:27:35,500 --> 00:27:37,700
End of the week, you get paid.

301
00:27:52,800 --> 00:27:54,100
Hey, Phil.

302
00:27:56,200 --> 00:27:58,700
I'm putting up for the Cape St. George.

303
00:27:58,800 --> 00:28:00,900
I don't see no resemblance.

304
00:28:01,100 --> 00:28:05,400
We're both bald, we're both Polacks.
What the fuck else you need to know?

305
00:28:26,200 --> 00:28:28,100
Who's gonna work for me?

306
00:28:29,900 --> 00:28:33,300
-A different look for our boy.
-Perry Ellis or something.

307
00:28:33,600 --> 00:28:37,700
How would a just-rolled-out-of-bed-looking
motherfucker like you...

308
00:28:37,800 --> 00:28:39,500
know the designer?

309
00:28:41,500 --> 00:28:43,200
Okay, I'm guessing.

310
00:28:45,100 --> 00:28:46,900
It's a Joseph Abboud.

311
00:28:47,700 --> 00:28:50,600
He puts dark buttons instead of brass
on his blazers.

312
00:28:50,700 --> 00:28:52,600
That's the Abboud signature.

313
00:28:52,700 --> 00:28:57,500
You know what they call a guy who pays
that much attention to his clothes, right?

314
00:28:57,700 --> 00:28:59,000
A grown-up.

315
00:29:01,000 --> 00:29:02,300
We're up.

316
00:29:03,500 --> 00:29:06,400
-12-14, let's go.
-Copy, 11-34.

317
00:29:22,600 --> 00:29:24,900
-That's a first.
-Sweat from a checker.

318
00:29:59,300 --> 00:30:01,200
-You all right?
-Ready.

319
00:30:03,300 --> 00:30:05,800
Maybe you ought to set up an easel
on the sidewalk...

320
00:30:06,000 --> 00:30:08,700
-and do a sketch instead.
-I'm fine.

321
00:30:34,200 --> 00:30:38,300
-Anything I ought to know?
-Yeah. Use the city.

322
00:30:39,200 --> 00:30:42,400
Windows, mirrors, reflections,
anything like that.

323
00:30:45,600 --> 00:30:47,700
Stay on my frequency, hear?

324
00:30:51,700 --> 00:30:54,400
Vondopoulos should be coming out
of the garage on foot...

325
00:30:54,500 --> 00:30:56,600
-right about now.
-Copy that.

326
00:31:59,100 --> 00:32:02,600
Beadie Russell. She wasn't much
when we started, you know.

327
00:32:02,700 --> 00:32:04,600
But now she's got game.

328
00:32:27,500 --> 00:32:28,800
Thank you.

329
00:33:22,900 --> 00:33:26,000
12-14. I got him going into
a fifth floor room.

330
00:33:26,200 --> 00:33:28,400
Note the number
then get down to the lobby.

331
00:33:28,500 --> 00:33:31,200
-Wait on him there.
-Copy.

332
00:33:46,500 --> 00:33:49,800
She's got Vondopoulos in a room.
It could be a while.

333
00:33:50,400 --> 00:33:51,500
Copy.

334
00:34:02,700 --> 00:34:05,700
-All this shit's going out to chassis?
-That's what they tell me.

335
00:34:05,800 --> 00:34:08,700
We need a forklift. We're almost done here.

336
00:34:24,700 --> 00:34:28,200
12-14. Vondopoulos and another man,
middle-aged, blue suit...

337
00:34:28,300 --> 00:34:31,800
leaving the front door of the hotel.
They're just behind me. Copy?

338
00:34:31,900 --> 00:34:32,900
Copy.

339
00:34:34,500 --> 00:34:35,700
11-34.

340
00:34:35,800 --> 00:34:39,800
Subject and companion, blue suit,
leaving the hotel any moment now.

341
00:34:39,900 --> 00:34:41,900
Copy, we got the eyeball.

342
00:34:49,500 --> 00:34:52,200
The man with Vondopoulos
has got to be big.

343
00:34:52,900 --> 00:34:56,800
-I mean, look at that expensive suit.
-Yeah, with them buttons and all.

344
00:35:15,100 --> 00:35:16,900
We leave the Benz here?

345
00:35:18,700 --> 00:35:19,900
It's hot.

346
00:35:36,400 --> 00:35:39,400
They didn't come back to the Benz.
You got them down there?

347
00:35:39,500 --> 00:35:40,700
Negative.

348
00:36:33,400 --> 00:36:36,600
-You about done?
-These nine here still got to be stripped.

349
00:36:36,700 --> 00:36:39,100
-Harder than it looks.
-What ain't?

350
00:36:41,500 --> 00:36:45,300
-You hear how Moonshot got his name?
-Yeah, and I could give a fuck.

351
00:36:47,800 --> 00:36:49,800
Who was the room registered to?

352
00:36:50,300 --> 00:36:54,100
Stephen Rados.
He gave a Northwest D.C. address.

353
00:36:54,300 --> 00:36:57,600
Maybe that's the man with the good tailor.
Maybe not.

354
00:36:57,700 --> 00:37:01,300
We should run out the paper trail
on this guy, see what we turn up.

355
00:37:02,100 --> 00:37:05,600
As to our only tangible piece of progress
from the raids...

356
00:37:05,700 --> 00:37:08,400
what can we do for our friend White Mike?

357
00:37:08,800 --> 00:37:12,400
He rolls on his suppliers,
and he can walk with a long probation.

358
00:37:12,500 --> 00:37:16,000
-And we can move him, if he needs.
-Witness protection?

359
00:37:16,700 --> 00:37:20,700
Why have the feds with you if they're
not gonna step up every now and then?

360
00:37:21,300 --> 00:37:24,700
Wait a second. You're gonna give
a drug dealer a ride like that?

361
00:37:24,800 --> 00:37:26,300
What about Frank Sobotka?

362
00:37:26,400 --> 00:37:28,800
The feds took a shot at him and got nothing.

363
00:37:28,900 --> 00:37:30,300
Or so they tell me.

364
00:37:30,400 --> 00:37:33,400
The way I read it, they cared more
about busting up the union--

365
00:37:33,500 --> 00:37:37,200
Than anything else in the case.
If we came at Frank straight?

366
00:37:38,600 --> 00:37:41,400
You can't make him
any kind of specific offer yourself.

367
00:37:41,500 --> 00:37:45,000
Only I can do that, and only after
I get an okay from my front office.

368
00:37:45,100 --> 00:37:48,700
-She could plant the seed.
-There's no better messenger, Counselor.

369
00:37:51,400 --> 00:37:52,700
Take a shot.

370
00:37:53,700 --> 00:37:57,200
-You going to his house?
-The Union Hall. That's his house.

371
00:37:59,100 --> 00:38:01,200
Thanks for waiting, Brucie. Sorry I'm late.

372
00:38:01,300 --> 00:38:03,400
I shouldn't even be seen with you
at this point.

373
00:38:03,500 --> 00:38:05,800
I just wanna settle our business
while we still can.

374
00:38:05,900 --> 00:38:09,000
It ain't like I'm gonna get my hands
on more cash, obviously.

375
00:38:09,100 --> 00:38:11,000
The grain pier is dead.

376
00:38:12,700 --> 00:38:16,100
Half the votes we had lined up
are walking sideways now.

377
00:38:16,200 --> 00:38:17,700
They read the paper, Frank.

378
00:38:17,800 --> 00:38:21,800
So what? So I'm dirty.
The grain pier's still the grain pier, right?

379
00:38:21,900 --> 00:38:24,400
They ain't voting for me, Brucie!
It ain't about me!

380
00:38:24,500 --> 00:38:25,600
I'm not gonna lie.

381
00:38:25,800 --> 00:38:29,300
No one is gonna stand with us
now that the FBI is on you.

382
00:38:29,400 --> 00:38:31,600
-They're scared.
-Of what?

383
00:38:32,000 --> 00:38:33,700
They took the money, Frank.

384
00:38:33,800 --> 00:38:37,800
And now if they deliver the votes,
they figure the feds will be on them, too.

385
00:38:37,900 --> 00:38:39,500
I'm sorry, Frank.

386
00:38:40,000 --> 00:38:42,600
You find a way
of putting this FBI thing to bed...

387
00:38:42,700 --> 00:38:45,400
maybe we can come back the next session
with the grain pier.

388
00:38:45,500 --> 00:38:49,700
You'll have a couple of people down there
knowing they owe you a vote or two.

389
00:38:51,100 --> 00:38:54,800
I don't know what else to say. I don't.
I'm sorry, Frank.

390
00:38:58,200 --> 00:39:00,700
You know what the trouble is, Brucie?

391
00:39:04,200 --> 00:39:07,300
We used to make shit in this country.
Build shit.

392
00:39:09,500 --> 00:39:12,700
Now we just put our hand
in the next guy's pocket.

393
00:39:33,500 --> 00:39:37,800
Come on, you can't eat only olives.
Order something. Lamb or something.

394
00:39:38,200 --> 00:39:39,700
I'm not hungry.

395
00:39:44,300 --> 00:39:45,600
All this trouble.

396
00:39:49,800 --> 00:39:53,300
-So, our associates, they are strong?
-Yes.

397
00:39:53,600 --> 00:39:57,200
I don't worry about our people.
We can try to get them out before the trial.

398
00:39:57,300 --> 00:39:59,400
If not, they will stand for us.

399
00:40:00,500 --> 00:40:04,400
We have shown them too much.
There will be no more trouble.

400
00:40:05,300 --> 00:40:07,500
We must make certain of this.

401
00:40:08,200 --> 00:40:11,700
-Maybe there's another way.
-There is only one sure way.

402
00:40:12,000 --> 00:40:13,100
Hear me out.

403
00:40:13,200 --> 00:40:16,800
If I could guarantee
that Frank Sobotka and his nephew...

404
00:40:16,900 --> 00:40:18,600
would be silent...

405
00:40:19,500 --> 00:40:21,500
wouldn't you prefer that?

406
00:40:22,200 --> 00:40:24,000
But you cannot guarantee this.

407
00:40:24,100 --> 00:40:27,500
Frank's son,
the idiot who shot George in his store...

408
00:40:28,500 --> 00:40:31,000
he is going to jail for a long time...

409
00:40:31,800 --> 00:40:33,100
unless....

410
00:40:36,100 --> 00:40:39,500
There was a young clerk wounded that day
in the store.

411
00:40:40,300 --> 00:40:43,200
The prosecutors want to use him
as a witness.

412
00:40:43,400 --> 00:40:45,000
I know his family.

413
00:40:46,200 --> 00:40:48,800
Frank Sobotka will have his son back.

414
00:40:49,500 --> 00:40:53,000
If a man can have this,
why would he talk to the police?

415
00:40:53,400 --> 00:40:55,300
What about Frank's nephew?

416
00:40:55,400 --> 00:40:58,700
He is the idiot's cousin.
He wants the same thing as Frank.

417
00:40:58,800 --> 00:41:01,900
Anyway, I don't worry about Niko.

418
00:41:05,300 --> 00:41:07,400
You are fond of him, Spiros.

419
00:41:08,400 --> 00:41:10,300
You should've had a son.

420
00:41:11,000 --> 00:41:13,300
But then I would've had a wife.

421
00:41:24,100 --> 00:41:28,100
If this maggot doesn't post by midnight,
I'm gonna take it personal.

422
00:41:32,000 --> 00:41:34,700
The shitbird lives in his parents' basement.

423
00:41:37,900 --> 00:41:40,300
Where's a guy like that gonna run?

424
00:42:20,400 --> 00:42:23,000
You wanna go with Auntie Tasha? Come on.

425
